source.source: HYG v4.4 (Hipparcos-Yale-Gliese Database, D. Nash / astronexus)
source.epoch: ICRS/J2000 equinox; source astrometry primarily Hipparcos-2007 reduction, epoch J1991.25
source.sentinelDistDoc: dist == 100000.0 marks an unmeasurable/negative Hipparcos parallax; rows with it are dropped, not shipped.
source.hipSentinelDoc: hip == 0 means the row has no Hipparcos catalogue number.

galacticFrame.source: Hipparcos Catalogue vol. 1 §1.5.3 (ESA SP-1200, 1997); J2000 galactic frame constants shared by astropy and SOFA

panorama.title: The Milky Way panorama
panorama.longitudeConvention: l = 0 at the column centre, increasing leftward (sky seen from inside)
panorama.latitudeConvention: b = +90 at row 0, -90 at the last row

catalogRegistration.role: retained source record only; the photograph is registered astrometrically and owns visible stars

pointSourcePresentation.positionSource: licensed ESO photographic local maxima; no Google catalogue bytes
pointSourcePresentation.qualification: native fixed-size catalogue behavior collapsed into the prepared cubemap; point positions and colors remain ESO-derived

sky.qualification: source-photographed full sky sampled in ICRF through the J2000 galactic frame and the anchor-registered panorama; the scene registration carries the Arrokoth pole and epoch; Solar System objects in the mosaic are capture artefacts; no Sun is baked into the cubemap
sky.sceneRegistrationChain: galactic -> ICRF (J2000 constants) -> body-fixed (IAU pole and prime meridian at the epoch) -> ecliptic presentation frame

analyticRadialFit.qualification: Least-squares fit to annular red-channel means from the bound native 128 by 128 Sun texture; fitted values only, no source pixels.

distanceScaling.qualification: The opaque photospheric core is projected from the IAU nominal solar radius and the object catalog's mean heliocentric distance. The retained glow profile remains a visual presentation; the distance is not epoch-specific.

provenance.source: JPL Horizons fixed 2026-09-03 epoch. Revised pole from the bundled Porter paper Table 2. Its PDS XML gives an inconsistent earlier pole; the paper pole is used with arbitrary meridian and no precision spin-phase claim.
provenance.qualification: Computed Arrokoth Sun direction at 2026-09-03T00:00:00 TT, expressed in the ecliptic presentation frame (north up, Sun left at zero yaw) and in view space at the default camera pose.

controls.label: LORRI
controls.description: Taken 6,628 km from Arrokoth. Bright patches and the neck are visible in the original grayscale exposure. The photographed lighting is retained; unseen and grazing surfaces remain gridded.
controls.title: New Horizons close approach

controls.label: False color
controls.description: Near-infrared, red and blue bands reveal color differences across the two lobes. The mission team aligned the bands and matched their blur. This is false color, not a human-visible reconstruction, at 340 metres per native pixel; the grid marks unsupported coverage.
controls.summary: Near-infrared, red and blue bands show spectral differences at 340 metres per native pixel. This is false color; the grid marks unsupported coverage.
controls.title: New Horizons false color

controls.label: Modeled albedo
controls.description: Fitted from 30 New Horizons approach observations on 31 December 2018 and 1 January 2019. Grayscale shows the released albedo values. Uniform areas are unconstrained model fill; the archive supplies no coverage mask. This is a fitted surface model, not a global photograph.
controls.title: New Horizons LORRI albedo model

controls.label: Shape model
controls.description: Released New Horizons contact-binary shape: two overlapping closed lobe meshes. Southern surface detail is constrained by flyby imagery; the unseen side is a source model estimate. Revised pole from the bundled Porter paper Table 2. Its PDS XML gives an inconsistent earlier pole; the paper pole is used with arbitrary meridian and no precision spin-phase claim. The grid marks unmapped terrain.
controls.title: Published New Horizons shape
